_comment: English names for cards/actions whose `en` field in the community data still holds Chinese/Japanese. "derived" entries reuse the official English that the same Chinese name carries on other cards; "translated" entries had no precedent and were translated here. Merged over cards.json at load time. "traits" holds English for pilot trait text (`en`) and for the pilot trait NAME (`name`), either alone or both; `name` is display-only, because the mechanics matcher keys on the Chinese `trait` the card already carries. "boxes" renames entries in boxes.json, keyed by box key.

XPA-59.source: The card itself. Our scan prints ID 69 in the corner, and the publisher's PD Pilots v1.0 EN list has exactly three Combatants numbered A-69, A-70 and A-71 at 10 points each. The community data numbered them A-101 to A-103, which matches nothing: not the card, not the parts list, not the publisher's own card pages (369/370/371). OTTO's photo of the H2 box contents shows the same ID 69.

FPA-06-2.source: publisher card page id 362, reached by the QR code on the RDL Dune card itself. Both KeyHole pilots reach us named just "KeyHole" even though they are different cards (FPA-06 has the Aura/Electronic range trait, this one gains Low Profile inside an allied Aura). They were the only two cards in the whole pool sharing a name, which also made this the one card the API sweep could not have matched automatically.

ZPA-36.name: Adjustment
ZPA-36.en: · Once per round, during the Command Phase, the piloted Mech may spend 1 Command Token to restore 1 Link to an Ally Mech.
ZPA-36.source: publisher parts list, GoF Pilots En sheet (1.02), QR 36 'Adjustment'. Fixes the bundle's 'Cmmand Token' typo AND takes the official text's subject with it: ours read 'may consume', naming nobody, where the official names the piloted Mech. Two deliberate departures from the sheet - it writes 'Command Stage', a term that appears NOWHERE in the rulebook (the digests say 'Command Phase' 30 times and 'Command Stage' zero), so the rulebook's term is kept; and 'the' is added before 'piloted Mech' for grammar.

XPA-62.source: translated. No `name`: XPA-62 Seagull appears in NONE of the five championship-legal parts lists, so there is no publisher English for its trait name (高抛发射) to take.
